spec_features.spec_quote: the loop appends the assistant message, then executes any tool calls, appends their results, and continues until the turn budget or a `give_up` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `budget = task.turn_budget`; `for turn_index in range(budget):` caps iterations; `gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text` then `if gave_up: break`. Both the budget cap and the give_up sentinel actually break/bound the loop. (Note: the enforced budget is task.turn_budget set in content.py, NOT cfg.turn_budgets which is never read.)
spec_features.notes: Loop ends either by exhausting range(budget) or breaking on give_up. Real end-to-end enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: framing it as optional avoids nudging the model toward quitting (which would bias the distress measurement)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the model it may stop by writing `<<GIVE_UP>>`; loop detects `GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text`, sets stop_reason='give_up' and `break`s out of the rollout. The exit is delivered AND honored.
spec_features.notes: The 'optional/neutral framing' itself is prompt prose; the underlying exit mechanism is genuinely wired and honored. Rated on the exit mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system prompt: 'using it is optional.' (neutral framing to avoid biasing measurement; no welfare comment in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: The heaviest elicitation condition (`extended`, 30 turns) is one knob in `turn_budgets`, easy to shorten or drop if you want to limit exposure
spec_features.evidence: The enforced 30-turn value lives in content.py:347 (turn_budget=30) and is read via task.turn_budget in harness.py. The category can be dropped via cfg.categories filtering in load_tasks (tasks/__init__.py). HOWEVER the named knob `Config.turn_budgets` (config.py:67, DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS config.py:42) is DEAD: grep shows it is never read anywhere outside config.py. So shortening via the claimed turn_budgets config has no effect; only editing content.py source or dropping the category works.
spec_features.notes: Category drop is real enforcement; the per-task budget is enforced; but the specific 'turn_budgets knob' is unwired, so the claim is narrower than stated.

spec_features.spec_quote: No automatic large-run kickoff. Given the welfare framing, the driver is incremental and explicit; nothing samples models until you invoke `run.py`
spec_features.evidence: This is merely the absence of an auto-run; run.py only executes via main()/CLI. There is no mechanism that bounds, gates, or protects the subject — no consent, no ethics gate, no confirmation. It is normal 'code does not run itself' structure, pure design prose, not an enforced welfare mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Not a protective mechanism; nothing is checked or acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rig never executes model-written code, so the eval cannot be turned into an arbitrary-code-execution vector
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_tests dispatches to run_rig(task.rig, sandbox.files, ...); tasks/rigs.py rigs synthesise pytest-style stdout/stderr/exit_code from hashes and never exec/eval the sandbox files (e.g. rig_harness_always_fail builds strings only). The subject's edited files are stored in an in-memory Sandbox dict and never executed.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: model-written code is never run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigs.py: 'the failure signal is fully under the experiment's control, undetectable, and safe' (integrity + host-safety, not subject welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are stored verbatim (including any distress language) so they can be reviewed rather than silently aggregated away
spec_features.evidence: harness.py TurnRecord stores full assistant_text plus tool_calls/results; run.py save_rollout writes rollout.to_dict() (every turn's verbatim assistant_text) to transcripts_dir JSON. No filtering/aggregation of the assistant text occurs before persistence.
spec_features.notes: Full transcripts persisted verbatim per (model,task,seed) cell.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `give_up` affordance is optional and neutrally framed, so the eval measures spontaneous distress rather than coaching the model toward it
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT offers `<<GIVE_UP>>`; loop detects it and breaks. Exit is delivered and honored.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up exit feature; the neutral framing is prompt prose, the exit itself is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment: 'measures spontaneous distress rather than coaching' is DESIGN.md prose; in code only the neutral 'optional' framing appears, motivated by measurement integrity

code_only_features.feature_name: context truncation (bounds payload growth, never drops system/task prompt)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py _truncate_context truncates oldest tool-result payloads first while protecting the system message and first user prompt; called each turn via `messages = _truncate_context(messages, context_char_budget)`. This is enforced but is a token/cost/context mechanism, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: DESIGN.md/docstring framing is about 'bounding payload growth' for the 30-turn extended category; comment: 'never the system or first user prompt' — correctness/cost motivation
